title: Centrifuge Whole Blood to Separate Red Blood Cells
author: George Lykotrafitis
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zzwf77e

steps.title: First centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the whole blood at 500 ×g, 4 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Remove plasma and buffy coat
steps.instruction: Carefully aspirate and discard the plasma layer and the buffy coat.

steps.title: Add Alsever's solution (first addition)
steps.instruction: Add Alsever's solution in a volume equal to the remaining blood components (red blood cells).

steps.title: Second centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the mixture again at 500 ×g, 4 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Remove the top layer (supernatant) without disturbing the cell pellet.

steps.title: Add Alsever's solution (second addition)
steps.instruction: Add Alsever's solution in a volume equal to the remaining blood components.

steps.title: Third centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge a third time at 500 ×g, 4 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add Alsever's solution and store
steps.instruction: Add Alsever's solution in a volume equal to the remaining red blood cells, then store the suspension at 4 °C for up to 7 days.
